source: Authored from `llama-server --help` of ggml-org/llama.cpp build b10566 (v0.2.0-dev). Regenerate against your own image with tools/gen_llamacpp_schema.py, which scrapes the same output.

sections.common params: Flags every llama.cpp tool shares: model loading, GPU offload, context, batching and the KV cache.
sections.sampling params: Server-wide sampling defaults. Every one of these is also overridable per request, so these are the values a client gets when it says nothing.
sections.speculative params: Draft-model speculative decoding. A second, smaller model proposes tokens the main model verifies in one pass.
sections.example-specific params: Flags that exist only for llama-server: the HTTP frontend, slots, chat templating and the endpoints it exposes.

args.help: Logical batch: how many prompt tokens are submitted at once before being split into physical batches.
Element type of the K half of the KV cache. q8_0 halves it against f16 for very little quality; q4_0 halves it again and is noticeable.
Element type of the V half. Anything other than f32/f16 needs flash attention; llama.cpp turns it on for you unless you turned it off.
Keep all mixture-of-experts weights on the CPU. On a sparse model this frees most of the file's bytes for a small speed cost, because only a few experts run per token.
Context length in tokens; 0 takes the model's own trained length. This is the single largest memory decision after --n-gpu-layers: the KV cache is linear in it.
Devices to use, comma separated, as named by --list-devices. 'none' offloads nothing.

Measure the real buffer sizes before loading and reduce --n-gpu-layers (and --ctx-size, if it was left at 0) until they fit. Only touches parameters still at their defaults, so an explicit -ngl opts out.
The smallest context --fit is allowed to settle on. It is a floor the fitting pass interpolates upward from, not a target.
MiB per device to leave free when --fit is on.

Fused attention. It does not change the KV cache's size, but it avoids materialising the attention-score matrix, which is what makes the compute buffer grow with context. Required for a quantised V cache.
Which file inside --hf-repo to use, overriding the quant chosen from the repo suffix.

A Hub repo as <user>/<model>[:quant] to download and serve. The quant suffix is case-insensitive and defaults to Q4_K_M, or the first GGUF in the repo. Set by the dashboard when the Model field names a repo.
Tokens from the start of the prompt to keep when the context shifts.
How the weights are read. Replaces --mmap/--mlock/--direct-io, which are kept only as deprecated aliases.
GGUF LoRA adapters to apply. These are converted adapters, not the PEFT directories the Fine-tune tab writes.
Adapters with a scale each, as FILE:SCALE.
Which device holds the small tensors and, under --split-mode none, the whole model.
Deprecated in favour of --load-mode. Lock the weights in RAM so they are never paged out.
Deprecated in favour of --load-mode. Memory-map the weights instead of reading them into RAM.
Path to the .gguf file to serve. Set by the dashboard from the Model field.
Download the model from this URL instead of a path or a Hub repo.
Keep the expert weights of this many layers on the CPU.

How many layers to hold in accelerator memory: a number, 'auto', or 'all'. llama.cpp offloads the LAST N of the model's layers plus one standing for the output head, so N counts down from the output rather than up from the embedding. 'auto' lets llama.cpp measure and fit; an explicit number disables that fitting and is attempted exactly.
Server-wide cap on generated tokens; -1 is unlimited.
NUMA placement strategy. Only meaningful when layers stay on the CPU.
Per-tensor device overrides as <regex>=<device>, comma separated.
RoPE base frequency. Unset takes the model's own.
RoPE frequency scaling, the reciprocal of --rope-scale.
Context scaling factor: 2 halves the frequency, doubling the reach.
How to stretch the model past its trained context. Unset takes whatever the GGUF header declares.
How to split the model across several accelerators. 'layer' gives each device whole layers; 'row' splits individual tensors and costs more traffic; 'none' keeps everything on --main-gpu.
Allocate a full-size cache for sliding-window attention layers instead of the window. Costs memory; needed for some reuse paths.
Proportions to split across devices, comma separated: 3,1 puts three quarters on the first device. Defaults to the devices' free memory.
CPU threads used during generation. -1 picks a count from the machine.
CPU threads used during prompt processing. Defaults to --threads.
Physical batch: how many tokens are computed in one pass. This is what actually sizes the compute buffer, so lower it first when a launch runs out of memory during prompt processing.
YaRN magnitude scaling for attention.
YaRN low-correction dimension.
YaRN high-correction dimension.
YaRN extrapolation mix; 0 is pure interpolation, -1 takes the model's.
The context the model was actually trained on, for YaRN scaling.
What clients put in the "model" field, and what /v1/models reports. Set by the dashboard from Served name.
Require this key in Authorization. Comma-separate to accept several.
A file of accepted API keys, one per line.
Reuse the KV cache of a prompt prefix a slot has already processed.
Smallest chunk of a cached prompt worth reusing by shifting the KV cache. 0 disables it.
A built-in template name, or the template's text, overriding the model's. Only well-known names are accepted unless --jinja is on.
A file holding the Jinja chat template to use instead of the model's.
A JSON object of extra variables handed to the chat template — this is where a model's own thinking switch usually lives.
Insert new requests into a batch already running instead of waiting for it to finish.
When a conversation outgrows the context, drop the oldest tokens and carry on rather than failing the request.
Norm applied to embeddings: -1 none, 0 max-abs, 1 taxicab, 2 euclidean.
Serve /v1/embeddings. An embedding server answers no chat endpoint.
Address to bind. Managed by the dashboard, which binds 0.0.0.0.
Ceiling on the tokens one image becomes.
Floor on the tokens one image becomes.
Render chat with the model's own Jinja template. Turning it off falls back to a built-in template and loses tool calling.
Share one context-sized KV pool across slots instead of giving each slot a fixed slice. On by default when the slot count is auto. The total the cache costs is the same either way.
Load the adapters but leave them off until POST /lora-adapters turns them on.
Expose Prometheus metrics on /metrics. Turned on by the dashboard, because the Metrics tab has nothing to read without it.
The multimodal projector file that lets this model take images.
Load the projector a multimodal repo ships alongside its weights. Turning it off (--no-mmproj) serves the model as text-only.
Keep the projector in accelerator memory.
Download the projector from this URL.

How many requests the server holds slots for. -1 is auto, which means four slots sharing one unified context. Slots divide the context rather than multiplying it, so more slots means less context each.
Directory of static files to serve alongside the API.
How token vectors become one vector. Unset takes the model's own.
Port to bind. Managed by the dashboard from the Port field.
Continue a trailing assistant message rather than starting a new turn.
Allow POST /props to change server properties at runtime.
Whether the model is asked to reason at all, for models that can be told.
Token ceiling on reasoning; -1 is unlimited, 0 disables it.
How much reasoning to ask for, on models that expose the setting.
How reasoning text is returned: 'none' leaves it inline in the content, 'deepseek' splits it into a reasoning_content field.
Serve /reranking for a cross-encoder model.
Directory where slot KV state is saved and restored.
Expose /slots, which reports what each request slot is doing.
Seconds between keep-alive pings on a streaming response; -1 disables.
PEM certificate for HTTPS.
PEM private key for HTTPS.
Threads serving HTTP. -1 derives one from the slot count.
Seconds before an idle HTTP connection is dropped.
Serve llama.cpp's own browser UI at the root path.
Longest repeated sequence DRY leaves unpenalised.
DRY penalty base.
DRY repetition penalty strength; 0 disables it.
How far back DRY looks, in tokens; 0 disables it. Must not be negative — llama-server rejects a negative value while parsing and exits.
Penalty proportional to how often a token was used.
A GBNF grammar the output must satisfy.
A file holding the GBNF grammar.
A JSON Schema the output must satisfy, compiled to a grammar.
Drop tokens below this fraction of the most likely one's probability.
Mirostat version: 0 off, 1 or 2 to target a perplexity.
Mirostat target entropy.
Mirostat learning rate.
Flat penalty on any token already used.
How far back the repetition penalty looks, in tokens; 0 disables it. Must not be negative — llama-server rejects a negative value while parsing its arguments and exits before the model is read.
Penalty on repeated tokens; 1 disables.
The sampler chain, semicolon separated, in the order it is applied.
Sampling seed; -1 is random per request.
Sampling temperature.
Keep only the k most likely tokens; 0 disables.
Keep tokens within n standard deviations of the top logit.
Keep the smallest set of tokens whose probability sums to p.
Locally typical sampling; 1 disables.
Chance of dropping a likely token, for variety; 0 disables.
Probability above which XTC may drop a token.
A small model that drafts tokens for the main one to verify. It must share the main model's tokenizer.
Most tokens to draft in one step.
Fewest tokens worth drafting before it is not worth the pass.
Layers of the draft model to offload. Its weights come out of the same pool as the main model's.
Stop drafting when the draft model's confidence falls below this.
Probability at which a draft splits into a tree.
Which speculation strategy to use — a draft model, or one of the n-gram methods that need no second model.
